chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qarashi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Sa'dan narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I said to Abu Abdullah

I said: A man who believes in the guardianship of Ali and exempts himself from his enemy, and believes in everything that he says, except that he says: They have disagreed among themselves whereas they are the leading imams. I do not know which of them is the Imam. If they agree upon a certain one, I will submit to his word, and I have known that the authority is among them. He (peace be upon him) said: If this man dies upon that state, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah). Then he said: The Qur'an has interpretations that occur as the day and the night run, and as the sun and the moon run. If an interpretation of something from it comes, it will occur. Some of it has come, and some of it has not come yet.

key_terms.مِيتَةَ جَاهِلِيَّةٍ: Death of ignorance (pre-Islamic state of disbelief)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on doubting the identity of the Imams and what does the Qur'an's ta'wil mean?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) elevates the doubt of the specific Imamate identity to a state of 'death of ignorance' (mawt al-jahiliyyah), emphasizing that mere general belief in the Twelve is insufficient without certainty in their leadership. This ruling underscores the Shia doctrine of *Ismah* and the necessity of recognizing the designated successor, contrasting with the ambiguity of the early Caliphate era. Furthermore, the hadith elucidates the dynamic nature of *Ta'wil* (esoteric interpretation), likening it to celestial cycles to illustrate that divine truths unfold progressively, with some aspects realized and others awaiting the advent of the Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (17) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Abu Ja’far al-Hamadani from Musa bin Sa’dan from Muhammad bin Sinan from Ammar bin Marwan that Suma’a bin Mihran had said: I said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as):

Someone believes in the guardianship of Ali (as) and exempts himself from Ali’s enemy. He believes in everything that Ali (as) has said but he says: They have disagreed among themselves whereas they are the leading imams. I do not know which of them is the imam. If they agree upon a certain one, I will submit to him. I have believed that the imamate is among them. Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) said: “If this someone still thinks so, he will die as an unbeliever. The Qur’an has interpretations that occur as the day and the night and they run as the sun and the moon. If an interpretation of something comes, it will occur. Some interpretations have come and some have not come yet.”
